test_the_fit.positive_self_check: This may fit if you trust documented rules, precedent, enforceable fairness, and institutions that prevent harm before crisis.
test_the_fit.tension_failure_mode: Watch for this tension: It distrusts private exceptions, impulsive intervention, and justice that cannot be made legible to everyone.
test_the_fit.certified_boundary_self_check: A rule-breaker, secret broker, or battlefield protector is not necessarily Azorius; the distinguishing question is whether public procedure remains the accountable method.

how_this_plays.how_opponents_read_it: A rule-setting Azorius list can ask opponents to plan around visible taxes, held mana, or timing constraints; the actual experience depends on the cards, pilot, and pod.

how_this_plays.lore_role: senate, judiciary, and lawkeeping bureaucracy

what_to_look_for.title: Public Rule-Setting
what_to_look_for.copy: Use visible taxes and restrictions to establish which actions remain available, with the rule serving an accountable table plan rather than delay for its own sake.

what_to_look_for.title: Procedural Permission
what_to_look_for.copy: Hold mana and answer the spell that changes the table, making careful systems and enforceable procedure the reason for restraint.

what_to_look_for.title: Timed Enforcement
what_to_look_for.copy: Act at the declared window, protect the board that follows the rule, and use Addendum-like timing as procedural texture instead of generic control proof.

test_the_fit.positive_self_check: This may fit if you observe first, control disclosure, value anonymity, and prefer advantage that does not require public credit.
test_the_fit.tension_failure_mode: Watch for this tension: It resists transparency as an automatic virtue and visible legitimacy as the only valid form of power.
test_the_fit.certified_boundary_self_check: Control, mill, theft, and evasive play do not establish Dimir by themselves; secrecy or information asymmetry must be the active method.

how_this_plays.how_opponents_read_it: Opponents rarely know which card matters until it has already taken their best line away.

what_to_look_for.copy: Turns knowledge, ambition, and patient growth into a plan that scales before it reveals itself.

what_to_look_for.title: Sterile Control Risk
what_to_look_for.copy: Carries the shadow risk of excluding impulse so completely that living growth becomes control.

test_the_fit.positive_self_check: Choose this path when limiting the commander's color identity and legal card pool is part of the appeal, not merely the price of playing artifacts or Eldrazi.
test_the_fit.tension_failure_mode: The restriction cuts both ways: utility lands compete with dependable {C} sources, and familiar colored answers are unavailable even when the deck needs them.
test_the_fit.certified_boundary_self_check: Look elsewhere if the draw is only generic costs, an artifact theme, Devoid, Phyrexia, or five-color Eldrazi. None of those establishes strict Colorless identity, and Colorless is not superior to or more complete than WUBRG.

how_this_plays.how_opponents_read_it: Opponents usually see mana infrastructure first, then learn whether the payoff is artifact machinery, a colorless nonartifact engine, or Eldrazi scale.
how_this_plays.emotional_pressure: The table must decide whether a mana piece is expendable or load-bearing; waiting for the expensive payoff can let the engine compound, while early removal may miss the card that matters.
how_this_plays.lore_role: Vox Mana treats Colorless as a bounded expression outside the five-color grammar, not an official Magic philosophy and not metaphysical nothingness.
how_this_plays.mechanical_expression: Wastes and other true {C} sources support a plan that may use artifact engines, colorless nonartifact cards, or Eldrazi. Those categories can share a deck without defining one another.
how_this_plays.table_experience: a resource-development opening that branches into machinery, nonartifact colorless payoffs, or enormous creatures rather than one prescribed archetype

what_to_look_for.title: Chosen Restriction
what_to_look_for.copy: Treats the empty Commander color identity and narrower legal card pool as the puzzle, never as superiority or completeness.

what_to_look_for.title: Machine And Void
what_to_look_for.copy: Compares artifact engines, colorless nonartifact cards, Wastes, and Eldrazi as separate deck directions; none proves the others.

what_to_look_for.title: Boundary Discipline
what_to_look_for.copy: Separates generic costs from true {C}, then checks colored symbols, color indicators, and Devoid before deciding Commander legality.

test_the_fit.positive_self_check: This may fit if access to White, Blue, Black, Red, and Green materially serves your commander, tribe, mechanic, theme, toolbox, or payoff.
test_the_fit.tension_failure_mode: Watch for this tension: broad color access asks more of the mana base and consistency, while the deck still needs a specific reason for being Five-Color.
test_the_fit.certified_boundary_self_check: This is less likely to fit when a narrower color identity serves the plan, or when all-five access is treated as proof of superiority, completion, or universal mastery.

how_this_plays.role: The commander determines the deck's engine, tribe, payoff, or tool suite; Five-Color supplies the access that plan needs.
how_this_plays.how_opponents_read_it: The commander often shows what all-five access is for—whether that is a tribe, toolbox, engine, payoff, or broad interaction suite.
how_this_plays.emotional_pressure: Five-Color can create uncertainty through breadth because several kinds of tools may be available; the actual engine determines where that pressure comes from.
how_this_plays.lore_role: Five-Color has represented tribes spanning the color pie, coalitions, magical breadth, multicolor systems, rainbow imagery, and other context-specific ideas. Vox Mana treats coalition, integration, and synthesis as possible readings rather than universal doctrine.
how_this_plays.mechanical_expression: Direct Five-Color mechanics ask you to assemble or spend all five colors. Other builds use broad access for color-count payoffs, land-type engines, multicolor systems, typal reach, or toolbox breadth.
how_this_plays.table_experience: Once the mana works, the table experience follows the deck's actual reason for being Five-Color: assembling a rainbow payoff, accessing a whole tribe, integrating multiple color roles, or drawing from a broader toolbox.

what_to_look_for.title: Full-Spectrum Integrator
what_to_look_for.copy: Optional Vox Mana archetype: coordinates distinct color contributions or requirements into one coherent plan without defining every Five-Color deck.

what_to_look_for.title: Five-Color Toolbox
what_to_look_for.copy: Uses broad color access to assemble answers or effects selected by a particular commander or deck plan.

what_to_look_for.title: Five-Color Typal
what_to_look_for.copy: Uses all five colors because a creature type, commander, or typal payoff spans the color pie.

what_to_look_for.title: Rainbow Payoffs
what_to_look_for.copy: Uses cards that reward assembling, spending, controlling, or representing several or all five colors, including WUBRG, sunburst, converge, color-count, or all-five requirements.

semantic_model.identity_floor: Five-Color means access to White, Blue, Black, Red, and Green at the Commander deck-construction layer; it does not supply one universal motive, role, metaphysics, or play pattern.
semantic_model.hero_anchor: All five colors are available. What brings them together depends on the deck.
